cards.a: A membrane-enclosed sac of digestive enzymes.

cards.q: What does the name lysosome mean?
Where are lysosome enzymes and membranes made?
cards.a: Made by rough ER, then processed in the Golgi.
Their enzymes work best in acid. The membrane keeps them away from the rest of the cell.
A membrane sac formed when a cell engulfs food particles.

cards.q: How do lysosomes help digest food?
cards.a: They fuse with a food vacuole and digest it; nutrients go into the cytosol.

cards.q: How do white blood cells use lysosomes?
cards.a: They engulf bacteria and destroy them with lysosome enzymes.

cards.q: How is a lysosome like a recycling center?
cards.a: It breaks down damaged organelles and old cytosol so the molecules can be reused.

cards.q: What is a lysosomal storage disease?
cards.a: An inherited disease where a lysosome enzyme is missing, so undigested material builds up.

cards.q: What goes wrong in Tay-Sachs disease?
cards.a: A lipid-digesting enzyme is missing, so lipids build up and harm brain cells.
